x-notifications.name: attach.hello
x-notifications.connection-state: first frame only, before raw terminal bytes
x-notifications.description: attach.sock begins with a frontend-to-daemon attach.hello notification (no id); named and ordered version,rows,cols,terminal,replay positional parameters retain the existing Serde forms; replay is optional vt (default) or snapshot, and any other value is an invalid hello. After structural decoding the daemon checks version 1 first (unsupported-version diagnostic), then refuses rows or cols outside 1..1000, the sessions.start/resize range, with the attach-size diagnostic before any attachment is reserved. A supplied terminal still requires 1..500 dimensions during target attachment, after the existing state/policy checks. Hello has a 4 KiB body and 3-second frame deadline, eight pending hellos per goblin and at most four accepts per tick. The daemon reads exactly the hello frame and consumes no following raw bytes.

x-notifications.name: attach.waiting
x-notifications.description: While startup or required onAttach variables are pending, the daemon sends attach.waiting with a required missing array, initially/periodically at one-second intervals. Empty missing means startup/draining; nonempty names identify variables that must be fresh and nonempty this run. A live competing attachment refuses without resizing. An exited onAttach client retains its physical stream until the frontend closes; new hellos receive empty waiting notices during that drain.

x-completions.name: attach.reply
x-completions.description: Completion after a valid modern hello and any waiting notifications. Modern attach.sock and legacy terminal.sock complete with a correlated JSON-RPC response of id 0: result attached=true, or error -32009 with a diagnostic. Only success switches the stream to raw bytes. terminal.sock is server-first with no hello; it keeps a stopped payload's screen until the terminal can be evicted, waits for configuration/readiness and refuses onAttach goblins with an upgrade message. The goblin's own terminal and named terminals are emulated: after success the stream carries a redraw of the screen, at the attachment's size on attach.sock and at the current size on terminal.sock, then live output while the program runs. Named-terminal attachments answer at once without waiting notices. onAttach clients get raw output without a redraw. With replay snapshot on attach.sock the redraw is replaced by a 4-byte big-endian length and that many bytes of libghostty-vt binary snapshot, taken before the resize; an onAttach client's has length 0. A screen that cannot be encoded (an unfinished escape sequence over the 64 KiB continuation limit) refuses the snapshot attachment with -32009 before acceptance or resize. The generic runtime Terminal::attach retains its private caller-supplied id (including nonzero test ids); public entrypoints pass 0. Byte queues, refusal-before-resize, descriptor ownership, cancellation and framed/raw boundaries remain handwritten.
